precepts.text: Joseph is blessed with the precious things put forth by the moon.
precepts.point: The moon is an instrument of the armies above.

note.label: Pope Nicholas & the Moors of Spain

precepts.why:
Moses blesses Joseph: “Blessed of the Lord be his land, for the precious things of heaven, for the dew, and for the deep that coucheth beneath,” “And for the precious fruits brought forth by the sun, and for the precious things put forth by the moon”. Joseph's sons, Ephraim and Manasseh, dwell on islands: the Puerto Ricans and the Cubans, among others.

The precious things of heaven are the rain; the deep that coucheth beneath is the oceans that give riches beneath the waters. There are certain fruits brought forth by the sun, and certain things that come forth only by moonlight on those islands, like the coquí frog, which is nocturnal and comes out especially under the moonlight, making its noise.

That blessing points to the moon at its peak, what they call the full moon today, which is actually the new moon. That is what leads into Ecclesiasticus 43:6: “He made the moon also to serve in her season for a declaration of times, and a sign of the world.”

precepts.text: The feasts of the Lord, starting with the Sabbath, are his appointed times.
precepts.point: The moon is an instrument of the armies above.

note.label: Pope Nicholas & the Moors of Spain

precepts.why:
The moon serves “in her season for a declaration of times”. Leviticus 23 shows what those times are: “Speak unto the children of Israel, and say unto them, Concerning the feasts of the Lord, which ye shall proclaim to be holy convocations, even these are my feasts.” Convocations means gatherings.

The first holy day God tells Moses to list is the Sabbath: “Six days shall work be done: but the seventh day is the sabbath of rest”, instituted from Genesis 2. Then: “These are the feasts of the Lord, even holy convocations, which ye shall proclaim in their seasons.” He did not say seasons for the Sabbath, because the Sabbath is all year round. The ones that follow are seasonal holy days.

“In the fourteenth day of the first month at even is the Lord’s passover”, in the spring. Then the feast of unleavened bread on the fifteenth day; Pentecost, counting fifty days; “In the seventh month, in the first day of the month, shall ye have a sabbath, a memorial of blowing of trumpets”, which is the seventh new moon celebration; the day of atonement on the tenth day of the seventh month; and “The fifteenth day of this seventh month shall be the feast of tabernacles”.

So the “declaration of times” is the high holy days. “From the moon is the sign of feasts”: every feast is counted from the new moon, when it is in its brightness, because that is how it was in the kingdom.

precepts.text: Esau is the end of the world and Jacob the beginning of what follows.
precepts.point: The moon is an instrument of the armies above.

note.label: Pope Nicholas & the Moors of Spain

precepts.why:
What is “a sign of the world”? One answer given from 2 Esdras 6:9, that Esau is the end of the world and Jacob the beginning of the world that follows, is that the sign of the world goes into our rulership and their destruction. That is not 100% wrong, and it should not be discounted.

The fuller understanding is this. The moon at its full is when we were in our full power and full understanding, in the kingdom. As it wanes and gets dark, it is us going into captivity, into full darkness. And once it gets back to fullness, it is us going back into our glory, back into the kingdom. That is the passing from Esau's world to Jacob's.

The moon's phases represent the stages the world is in: “a light that decreaseth in her perfection”, “increasing wonderfully in her changing”. And in the kingdom it will not wane again: “the light of the moon shall be as the light of the sun”, and the sun has no phases. When Jacob's world follows Esau's, there is no going back into darkness.

precepts.text: Darkness covers the earth and gross darkness the people until Israel's light comes.
precepts.point: The moon is an instrument of the armies above.

note.label: Pope Nicholas & the Moors of Spain

precepts.why:
“Arise, shine; for thy light is come, and the glory of the Lord is risen upon thee.” Arise means wake up; shine means teach; and the light that is come is Christ, who said, I am the light. “For, behold, the darkness shall cover the earth, and gross darkness the people”. We are in the grossest of darkness; we have lost our heritage and lost everything. When you see the moon dark, that is what it represents: darkness has covered the whole world.

Psalms 82 shows the same darkness. “God standeth in the congregation of the mighty; he judgeth among the gods.” The little g is us. Asaph, with the Holy Spirit upon him, records what we did wrong as the gods of the earth: “How long will ye judge unjustly, and accept the persons of the wicked?” We were to defend the poor and fatherless and deliver the needy, but “they walk on in darkness: all the foundations of the earth are out of course.” “I have said, Ye are gods; and all of you are children of the most High.” “But ye shall die like men”: our godhood was taken from us. “Arise, O God, judge the earth: for thou shalt inherit all nations.”

Something in the heavens is out of course because of our sins. God made “two great lights; the greater light to rule the day, and the lesser light to rule the night”. But in the kingdom, Isaiah 30:26: “Moreover the light of the moon shall be as the light of the sun, and the light of the sun shall be sevenfold, as the light of seven days, in the day that the Lord bindeth up the breach of his people, and healeth the stroke of their wound.” The sun has no phases; in the kingdom the moon, the sign of the world, will not go dark again. And the sun we call so bright is not bright at all next to that.

Binding up the breach is Amos 9:11: “In that day will I raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen, and close up the breaches thereof”, gathering the twelve tribes of Israel back again. That is when Isaiah 60:1 is fulfilled: our light is come, the moon is back at its fullness, and Israel is back in the kingdom.

precepts.text: Look upon the rainbow and praise Him that made it; the hands of the Most High bended it.
precepts.point: The world has taken that same bow, the token of the covenant, and turned it into the symbol of sodomy. The spiritual eyes will see what that means: the great city is spiritually called Sodom and Egypt.

note.label: Genesis 9: The Laws Before Moses and the Covenant of the Bow

precepts.why:
The bow in the cloud, the rainbow, is the token of the covenant between the Most High and the earth. “Look upon the rainbow, and praise him that made it; very beautiful it is in the brightness thereof. It compasseth the heaven about with a glorious circle, and the hands of the most High have bended it.”

His hands bended it. When you see the bow you are to praise Him that made it, and remember the covenant it stands for.

precepts.text: The moon serves for a declaration of times, and from the moon is the sign of feasts; the month is called after her name.
precepts.point: If the new moon falls on a seventh day Sabbath there is absolutely no cooking; the only day that permits cooking on the Sabbath is the Passover.

note.label: Leviticus 23: The Feasts of the Lord

precepts.why:
“In the seventh month, in the first day of the month, shall ye have a sabbath, a memorial of blowing of trumpets.” The first day of the month is the new moon, so the memorial of blowing of trumpets is a new moon; the seventh new moon is the special one, and that one is called the memorial of blowing of trumpets.

The Most High “made the moon also to serve in her season for a declaration of times, and a sign of the world. From the moon is the sign of feasts, a light that decreaseth in her perfection.” The moon is needed to calculate the feasts. “The month is called after her name, increasing wonderfully in her changing”: the new moon starts the new month, and she increases through her phases.

If the new moon falls on a seventh day Sabbath there is absolutely no cooking; the only day that permits cooking on the Sabbath is the Passover.

precepts.text: The moon declares the times and seasons and is the sign of feasts; her cycle marks the beginnings of the months.
precepts.point: The beginnings of the months are marked by the moon: the Most High made the moon to serve in her season for a declaration of times, a light that decreaseth in her perfection and then increaseth in her changing, and the month is called after her name. When the light is full again, that is the new moon.

note.label: Numbers 10: The Silver Trumpets and the Order of the Journeys

precepts.why:
The trumpets were blown “in the day of your gladness, and in your solemn days, and in the beginnings of your months”, over the burnt offerings and the peace offerings, “for a memorial before your God.” The beginnings of the months are marked by the moon.

“He made the moon also to serve in her season for a declaration of times, and a sign of the world. From the moon is the sign of feasts, a light that decreaseth in her perfection. The month is called after her name, increasing wonderfully in her changing.” The moon declares the times and seasons and is the sign of the feasts; her cycle marks the beginnings of the months. Her light decreases in her perfection and then increases in her changing, and when the light is full again, that is the new moon.

The feast days must be a glad moment even to this day. Coming to congregate with your brothers and sisters grudgingly is one of the reasons Israel went into captivity: we were not glad to do what the Most High said.

precepts.text: How shall we be able to magnify him, for he is great above all his works?
precepts.point: I will praise thee for ever, because thou hast done it; and I will wait on thy name, for it is good before thy saints.

note.label: Psalm 52: The Boasting Man of Sin Revealed

precepts.why: “I will praise thee for ever, because thou hast done it”. “How shall we be able to magnify him? for he is great above all his works.” He is great above all his works, so how can we magnify him enough? David's answer is to praise him for ever and wait on his name, for it is good before his saints.

precepts.text: When you glorify the Most High, exalt him as much as you can, for he far exceeds; put forth all your strength and be not weary, for you can never go far enough.
precepts.point: I will praise thee for ever, because thou hast done it; and I will wait on thy name, for it is good before thy saints.

note.label: Psalm 52: The Boasting Man of Sin Revealed

precepts.why:
“When ye glorify the Lord, exalt him as much as ye can; for even yet will he far exceed: and when ye exalt him, put forth all your strength, and be not weary; for ye can never go far enough.” Exalt the Most High as much as you can, for he far exceeds it; put forth all your strength and be not weary, for you can never go far enough.

That is why David says “I will praise thee for ever”. Praise for ever is the only fitting measure for one great above all his works, and waiting on his name is good before his saints.

precepts.text: The moon marks the seasons and the appointed feasts.
precepts.point: He makes darkness and it is night, wherein the beasts of the forest and the young lions seek their meat from God; the night belongs to the beasts, the day belongs to man who goes to his labor until evening.

note.label: Psalm 104: The Most High Clothed with Majesty over Creation

precepts.why:
“He appointed the moon for seasons”. Ecclesiasticus gives the reason: “He made the moon also to serve in her season for a declaration of times, and a sign of the world.”

“From the moon is the sign of feasts, a light that decreaseth in her perfection.” The moon does not only mark the seasons; it marks the appointed feasts of the Most High. That is the office he gave it in the creation, alongside the sun that “knoweth his going down”, the darkness he makes for the beasts of the forest and the day he gives to man for his labour until the evening.
